risks.risk_name: Inadequate Identity Verification for Financial Data Disclosure
risks.description: Customer financial data including loan account numbers, EMI amounts, payment history, and outstanding balances are disclosed to callers based solely on caller ID matching without additional identity verification. This creates risk of unauthorized access if someone else uses the customer's registered phone.
risks.evidence: The caller ID match from Ameyo is considered sufficient identification. If the call is from the registered mobile number, we assume it's the customer. We don't do an additional KYC on the call. Which, now that I think about it, could be an issue — someone else could be using the customer's phone.
risks.recommendation: Implement multi-factor authentication for phone-based customer verification before disclosing sensitive financial information, such as requiring customers to provide additional identifying information like loan account number or date of birth.

risks.risk_name: Excessive Access to Sensitive Complaint Data
risks.description: All customer care agents have unrestricted access to highly sensitive bribery complaint cases containing whistleblower information, employee allegations, and supporting evidence. This violates principle of least privilege and creates risk of data misuse or retaliation.
risks.evidence: All customer care agents can see all cases in the system. There's no restriction based on case category. So technically, a regular agent could open a bribery complaint case and see the details... I've raised this before but Salesforce configuration hasn't been updated.
risks.recommendation: Implement role-based access controls in Salesforce to restrict access to sensitive complaint categories. Only authorized personnel (Ethics team, management) should access bribery and sensitive complaint cases.

risks.description: Customer financial data including account details and personal information is accessible across multiple departments (Customer Care and Retention teams) without clear business justification for all access scenarios.
risks.evidence: And the customer's data — their account details, their stated reason for wanting to close — that's visible to both Customer Care and Retention? Yes, through Salesforce. Retention has access to the same customer records we do.
risks.recommendation: Review and implement data access controls based on business need-to-know principles. Limit cross-departmental access to only the minimum data required for specific business functions.

risks.description: Agents have immediate access to extensive customer financial profiles including loan amounts, payment history, overdue status, and co-applicant details without verification of legitimate business need for each data element during the interaction.
risks.evidence: The agent gets a Salesforce screen with the customer's profile. That includes — customer name, loan account number, registered mobile number, email address, loan product type, sanctioned amount, outstanding principal, EMI amount, next due date, payment history, overdue status if any, co-applicant details if there is one, and the branch that originated the loan.
risks.recommendation: Implement progressive data disclosure where agents only see basic customer information initially, with additional sensitive financial details revealed only when required for the specific customer interaction.

risks.risk_name: Broad Financial Data Exposure to Multiple Teams
risks.description: Comprehensive customer financial data including loan account numbers, sanctioned amounts, outstanding principal, EMI amounts, and payment history is accessible to both Customer Care and Retention teams through Salesforce, potentially beyond what's necessary for their respective functions.
risks.evidence: The agent gets a Salesforce screen with the customer's profile. That includes — customer name, loan account number, registered mobile number, email address, loan product type, sanctioned amount, outstanding principal, EMI amount, next due date, payment history, overdue status... Retention has access to the same customer records we do.
risks.recommendation: Review and implement data minimization principles by restricting each team's access to only the customer data elements necessary for their specific business functions.

risks.description: Customer data flows automatically between Ameyo IVR system and Salesforce without clear visibility into data handling controls, encryption, or access logging across the integration.
risks.evidence: Ameyo is integrated with Salesforce. When a call comes in, the system checks the caller's number against our customer database in Salesforce... Ameyo pulls up the customer profile from Salesforce and shows it on the agent's screen before they even pick up.
risks.recommendation: Conduct security assessment of the Ameyo-Salesforce integration including data encryption in transit, access logging, and ensure proper data handling controls are in place across both systems.

risks.risk_name: Cross-Department Data Access Without Business Justification
risks.description: Customer financial data including account details and closure reasons are accessible to both Customer Care and Retention teams through shared Salesforce access, potentially beyond what's necessary for each team's functions.
risks.evidence: And the customer's data — their account details, their stated reason for wanting to close — that's visible to both Customer Care and Retention? Yes, through Salesforce. Retention has access to the same customer records we do.
risks.recommendation: Review and implement principle of least privilege for cross-departmental data access, ensuring each team only has access to customer data necessary for their specific business functions.

risks.description: Extensive customer personal and financial information is displayed to agents immediately upon call connection, including co-applicant details and complete payment history, creating risk of unnecessary data exposure.
risks.evidence: The agent gets a Salesforce screen with the customer's profile. That includes — customer name, loan account number, registered mobile number, email address, loan product type, sanctioned amount, outstanding principal, EMI amount, next due date, payment history, overdue status if any, co-applicant details if there is one, and the branch that originated the loan. Plus any previous case history
risks.recommendation: Implement progressive data disclosure where agents only see customer data relevant to the specific inquiry, with additional details available on-demand based on the nature of the customer's request.
